title: Meta Content Library Community Roundtable – Where to for Social Media Research?
snippet: Program announcement for the 2026 International Conference on Social Media & Society in Glasgow. Professor Fabio Giglietto is featured as an expert panelist for a roundtable evaluating the opportunities and technical hurdles of using the Meta Content Library (MCL) API for public-interest research.
description: Fabio Giglietto is featured as a panelist for the 'Meta Content Library Community Roundtable' at the International Conference on Social Media & Society 2026.

title: Facebook, troppa visibilità a estremisti e complottisti: ecco come impatta Meta sulle elezioni
snippet: A news feature detailing the findings of Fabio Giglietto's research on Meta's algorithmic choices. The article highlights how democratic representatives lost a massive chunk of their digital reach due to algorithmic changes, while anti-establishment and vaccine-skeptical ecosystems thrived.
description: An article covering Professor Fabio Giglietto's research analyzing over 2.5 million Facebook posts, focusing on how political extremist pages bypassed Meta's filters to gain visibility during elections.

title: Secondo uno studio dell'università di Urbino l'algoritmo di Facebook ora punisce la politica ufficiale e premia gli estremisti antieuropei. Pd e FdI verso una legge bipartisan sulle piattaforme
snippet: Though slightly outside the strict six-month window (published in January 2026), this major national news article details Giglietto's breakthrough research. It reports on how his analysis of 2.5 million Facebook posts demonstrated significant transparency deficits in Meta's algorithmic filtering, prompting Italian lawmakers to discuss bipartisan regulations.
description: A major Italian news article covering a breakthrough study by Fabio Giglietto and his team at the University of Urbino, analyzing Facebook's algorithm and its impact on political content exposure.

title: Referendum. Bonelli e Fratoianni (Avs) scrivono al Presidente Agcom, preoccupati per le fake news veicolate sui social. Chiesto incontro.
snippet: This political press release reports on a formal letter sent to Italy's communication authority (AGCOM) regarding misinformation. The politicians explicitly cite Professor Fabio Giglietto's study on Meta's algorithmic filtering and its role in boosting political extremism as a key evidence-based driver for their official intervention.
description: Italian political leaders Bonelli and Fratoianni cite research by Fabio Giglietto in an official letter to AGCOM regarding social media manipulation and algorithm bias.
